catalogue.name: Inventory.Tracking.Get
catalogue.description: Les lotu-, raðnúmera- og pakkarakningu fyrir vöru eða skjalalínu.
catalogue.selectionDescription: Veldu uppruna eða eldri skjalalínuvalkost; annars skaltu velja vöru. SystemId sölu-, innkaupa- eða flutningslínu í subject velur þann uppruna.

subject.description: The subject is the SystemId of a Sales Line, Purchase Line or Transfer Line (selects that source) or the SystemId or No. of the Item; data selects the same things when subject is blank.

target.description: A Sales Line, Purchase Line or Transfer Line selected by type and systemId (and transferDirection). A source takes precedence over every other selector.

target.form: document type, document no. and line no.
target.description: A Sales Line, Purchase Line or Transfer Line selected by document type, document number and line number. It takes precedence over subject and item selectors.
The same line selected by its SystemId, with documentType instead of documentNo and lineNo.
The SystemId of a Sales Line, Purchase Line or Transfer Line selects that source; any other SystemId is read as the SystemId of the Item.
The No. of the Item; it takes precedence over the item identifiers in data.
The No. of the Item, used when subject is blank.
The SystemId of the Item, tried in this order after itemNo.
An Item table view; the first matching item is read, so filter to one item for an exact selection.

parameters.name: systemId
parameters.description: Item SystemId, or document line SystemId with documentType.

parameters.name: tableView
parameters.description: Business Central Item table view in SetView syntax. Item mode only, after subject and item identifiers; reads tracking for the first matching item. Filter to one item for an exact selection.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of rows to skip; default 0.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The source line to read tracking for. Source takes precedence over the legacy document fields.

children.name: type
children.description: SalesLine, PurchaseLine or TransferLine.

children.name: systemId
children.description: The SystemId (GUID) of the source line.

children.name: transferDirection
children.description: Outbound (default) or Inbound; selects the shipment or the receipt side of a TransferLine.

parameters.name: documentType
parameters.description: Sales.Order, Sales.Invoice, Sales.CreditMemo, Sales.ReturnOrder, Purchase.Order, Purchase.Invoice, Purchase.CreditMemo, Purchase.ReturnOrder or Transfer.Order. The unqualified Order, Invoice, Credit Memo and Return Order mean the Sales types. Quotes and blanket orders are not supported.

parameters.name: documentNo
parameters.description: Document number with documentType and lineNo, up to 20 characters. Not used when systemId selects the line.

parameters.name: lineNo
parameters.description: Positive document line number, with documentType and documentNo.

parameters.name: transferDirection
parameters.description: Outbound (default) or Inbound for transfers, with documentType Transfer.Order.

fields.name: itemNo
fields.description: Item on the selected source or item.

fields.name: quantityBase
fields.description: Sum of all matching signed tracking rows before paging; not available stock.

fields.name: sourceType
fields.description: Source mode only: the source kind, for example SalesLine, PurchaseLine or TransferLine.

fields.name: sourceTableNo
fields.description: Source mode only: the table number of the source line.

fields.name: sourceSubtype
fields.description: Source mode only: the document type ordinal of the source line, or the transfer direction.

fields.name: documentType
fields.description: Source mode only: the document type of the source line, for example Purchase.Order.

fields.name: sourceId
fields.description: Source mode only: the document number of the source line.

fields.name: documentNo
fields.description: Source mode only: the document number of the source line, as sourceId.

fields.name: sourceBatchName
fields.description: Source mode only: the batch name of the source line; blank for document lines.

fields.name: sourceProdOrderLine
fields.description: Source mode only: the production order line of the source line; 0 for document lines.

fields.name: sourceRefNo
fields.description: Source mode only: the line number of the source line.

fields.name: lineNo
fields.description: Source mode only: the line number of the source line, as sourceRefNo.

fields.name: trackingLines
fields.description: The tracking rows of the page: remaining ledger entries and nonzero reservation entries in item mode; reservation and tracking specification rows in source mode.

children.name: source
children.description: Where the row comes from: ItemLedgerEntry, ReservationEntry or TrackingSpecification.

children.name: entryNo

children.name: itemNo

children.name: serialNo

children.name: packageNo

children.name: variantCode

children.name: documentType

children.name: sourceId

children.name: documentNo
children.description: Reservation rows only: the document number of the source, as sourceId.

children.name: sourceBatchName

children.name: sourceProdOrderLine

errors.when: A required source or document identifier is absent.
errors.fix: Supply the required selector and data described in parameters.

errors.when: A source object, identifier, number, date, filter or array has an invalid type or range.
errors.fix: Use the declared JSON types and valid ranges.

errors.when: The source, pairing or tracking values are unsupported, the source is closed, or the company domain is disabled.
errors.fix: Correct the selection; check Inventory Setup and native source rules.

errors.when: A selected source is missing or no tracking rows match before paging.
errors.fix: Check the source and intersected filters; paging alone does not cause this error.

errors.when: The caller lacks required domain or native table permissions.
errors.fix: Ask an administrator for the required permissions.

errors.error: Native item selection or filter error.
errors.when: Foundation rejects the item selector or a native filter cannot be evaluated.
errors.fix: Correct the item selection and Business Central filter syntax.

effect.changes: Nothing is changed. Reads lot, serial and package tracking from item ledger entries, reservation entries and tracking specifications.

examples.title: Read the lot tracking of item 1000 at location BLUE

chapters.overview: Reads lot, serial and package tracking for an item or document line.
chapters.notes: Read only. Source selection takes precedence over item selection. Item mode returns tracked remaining ledger entries and nonzero reservation entries; source mode returns reservation and tracking specification rows. quantityBase totals all matching rows before paging, not available stock. Expiration is the native entry date only when Use Expiration Dates is enabled; otherwise blank, never 0D. No matching tracking returns RecordNotFound; paging past existing rows returns an empty page.

result.conventions:
## Errors and warnings
An error response has `status` = `Error`, a stable `code`, the `error` text and, when they apply, `parameter` (the request parameter concerned, e.g. `lines[2].no`), `received` (the value received), `expected` (what was expected) and `nextStep` (what to do now). `hint` says where to read more.
When a request has several problems, all of them are listed in `errors[]` - each with the same fields - under a top-level `code` (`MultipleErrors`, or a shared code such as `InvalidLine` for the `lines` of a Create type) and a summary `error`. Fix them all before calling again. One problem is reported at the top level, with no `errors[]`.
Request values are checked first and every problem found is reported together. A Business Central validation error raised afterwards, while a record is being written, stops the call and is reported on its own: `code` = `BusinessCentralError`, Business Central's own `error` text, and `parameter` naming the request parameter being applied, e.g. `lines[1].accountNo`. Nothing is written.
Request values are read in one format, whatever the language: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; date-times ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset; amounts as JSON numbers (or a string such as `"1234.56"`, no thousands separator); integers as JSON integers; booleans `true` or `false`. Any other value is `InvalidParameterFormat` with `received` and `expected`; for an unambiguous local form such as `26.09.2026`, `nextStep` gives the value to resend. Every bad value of a request is reported together.
Answers are written in one format as well, whatever the language of the call: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601, numbers with a dot and no thousands separator, and the option and enum values of every answer except `Data.Records.Get` and `Data.Records.Set` as their English names, so a value read from an answer can be sent back. Those two answer the caption of the language of the call, for a person to read. The language of the call (`lcid`) changes captions and message texts, not these forms. Two things are outside Bifrost's control: Business Central writes its own texts (a ledger entry description such as `Direct Cost V00010 on 10/02/26`, the text of a `BusinessCentralError`) with the regional settings of the server session, which `lcid` does not change, so a date in such a text can be in month-day order; and a table view is read with those settings too, so write dates in a view as `YYYY-MM-DD` and decimals with a dot.
Both success and error responses can carry `warnings[]`, each with `code`, `message` and, when they apply, `parameter` and `nextStep`.
`UnknownParameter` refuses undeclared data keys before execution for every type whose effect is not read, including a missing effect. The root envelope option `strict:false` cannot opt out. Read types keep warnings without changing status, validationResult or domain warningCount unless the caller sets `strict:true` (next to type and subject, never inside data). Refusals list the keys and localized nextStep corrections; no business changes or successful execution charges occur. Example: {"type":"Memory.User.Set","strict":true,"data":{"memory":"test","memry":"typo"}} is refused.
`FieldChangedByBC` is a warning from Data.Records.Set: another field validation or the write changed a sent field after its own validation. `parameter` names data[n].fields.{jsonName}, counting from 0. Status stays Success. Compare the returned values with what you sent; follow `nextStep` to use validation order or send the field again in a separate call. Normalisation of the field itself, LCY, Dimension Set ID, BLOB, Media, MediaSet and skipped fields are excluded.
When a Business Central operation fails, the error can identify the request parameter being applied, the expected input and what to do next. That guidance accompanies the original `BusinessCentralError` after rollback, including a failed queued task. It does not change which writes are rolled back or committed. Guidance is cleared between messages; a message without it keeps its existing response shape. Recognized lock errors follow the `Retryable` rules below.
Some message types accept calls only through a particular path: a scheduled queue message, the Task API (`/tasks`), the in-product MCP tool server, another message type, or the Messages page Run Task action. Bifrost determines where the call came from; request values cannot override it. A call through an unsupported path is refused with `PreconditionFailed` and a `nextStep` naming the path to use.
`Retryable` means a transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. `error` keeps Business Central's original text. `expected` is "no concurrent lock on the same records"; `nextStep` is "Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed." Bifrost does not retry automatically. Uncaught recognized lock errors are also `Retryable` for `write` types. Uncaught `read` and `irreversible` errors remain `BusinessCentralError`, because an irreversible operation may already have committed.
`ConfirmationRequired` is the preview refusal for an irreversible type called without `expectedCount`. Nothing was changed; inspect `expected` and the description before sending the same request with that count. `ConfirmationMismatch` means the count has changed or the sent count was wrong; nothing was changed. Inspect the new preview before confirming again. Feature apps use the same preview and confirmation protocol for irreversible operations.
Codes: `MissingParameter`, `InvalidParameterFormat`, `InvalidParameter`, `RecordNotFound`, `AmbiguousRecord`, `ConflictingIdentifiers`, `InvalidFilterField`, `InvalidLine`, `NothingToPreview`, `LinesSkipped`, `BlockedByWriteGuard`, `PreconditionFailed`, `PermissionDenied`, `LimitExceeded`, `BusinessCentralError`, `MultipleErrors`, `DeprecatedParameter`, `UnknownParameter`, `FieldChangedByBC`, `Retryable`, `EULA_REQUIRED`, `TRIAL_NOT_STARTED`, `ConfirmationRequired`, `ConfirmationMismatch`. The `error` text may be translated; the code never is.
